qs.q: An ophthalmology patient presenting with recurrent corneal ulcers undergoes a slit-lamp examination, which reveals pathognomonic branching dendritic lesions on the corneal epithelium. Which pathogen is responsible for this finding?
qs.e: Herpetic keratoconjunctivitis caused by HSV-1 typically presents with dendritic corneal ulcers upon recurrence, which can lead to permanent corneal scarring and blindness. Varicella-Zoster Virus can cause ophthalmic zoster, but dendritic ulcers are classically associated with HSV-1 keratitis.
